postData.contentHtml:
The Women's Rugby League World Cup witnessed a captivating clash as the New Zealand Kiwi Ferns fended off a spirited challenge from debutants Fiji, securing an 18-12 victory in a match that kept fans on the edge of their seats. What was expected to be a straightforward win for the experienced New Zealand side turned into a nail-biting encounter, showcasing the rapidly growing talent within international rugby league.

Fiji's Bulikula, making their historic first appearance in a World Cup, delivered a performance far exceeding expectations. Despite conceding an early try in the second minute, they refused to be intimidated, roaring back with two converted tries late in the first half. Their formidable defence and 'on fire' attacking prowess, as noted by commentators, consistently tested the Kiwi Ferns.

The second half was a tense battle, with both teams exchanging blows and resorting to penalty goals in crucial moments. New Zealand, surprisingly, opted for a penalty goal from close range at one point, a move commentators like Brett Kimmorley interpreted as 'a huge show of respect for how the opposition is defending.' While New Zealand leveled the scores, Fiji continued to press, even having a chance to retake the lead with a missed penalty goal from skipper Sereana Naitokatoka.

Ultimately, it was the Kiwi Ferns who held their nerve, converting a penalty goal to take a 14-12 lead with just under six minutes remaining, and then sealing the victory with a powerful run from Mele Hufanga setting up a try for Leianne Tufuga. However, Fiji's relentless spirit was evident until the very last seconds, almost snatching a dramatic comeback from a short kick-off.

New Zealand fullback Apii Nicholls acknowledged the intensity of the match, calling their error-strewn performance a 'wake-up call' and admitting they were 'caught off-guard' by the Fijians' speed and aggression. Despite the loss, Fiji captain Sereana Naitokatoka expressed immense pride in her team's 'amazing' and 'challenging' effort, attributing it to the 'Fijian blood inside of us' and their warrior spirit. Commentators hailed the game as one that 'no one will ever forget,' destined to 'go down in history' for Fiji's remarkable debut.

This thrilling contest not Mely highlights the competitive nature of the Women's Rugby League World Cup 2026 but also signals a bright future for nations like Fiji, who are rapidly making their mark on the global stage.
postData.title: New Zealand Avoids World Cup Shock as Fiji's Debut Shines
postData.summary: New Zealand's Kiwi Ferns narrowly escaped a major upset, securing an 18-12 victory over an impressive Fiji Bulikula in their Women's Rugby League World Cup debut. The thrilling encounter saw Fiji push the established New Zealand side to their limits, marking an unforgettable moment in the tournament.
